Contact lenses · Clear Lake

Contact lenses in Clear Lake, fitted by your own doctor.

Contact lenses are a medical device that sits on the eye all day, so the fit matters as much as the power. In Clear Lake, Dr. Hyder fits soft, toric, multifocal and gas-permeable contact lenses, checks how they sit on your cornea, and keeps a record of what actually worked for you.

Soft, toric, multifocal and gas-permeable fittingsTrial lenses to wear home, often the same dayYour fitting kept on file, so a repeat is straightforward
Schedule an Eye Exam Call (281) 488-0066

Lens pricing depends on your prescription and your plan, so we quote it in person. Call and we will check your coverage.

How a fitting works

Three things a contact lens fitting settles.

An eyeglass prescription is not a contact lens prescription. The lens sits directly on the eye, so it needs its own measurement and its own follow-up.

The measurement How the lens sits on your eye Curvature, diameter and how the lens moves when you blink. Get this wrong and a technically correct power still feels wrong all day.
Book an eye exam
The trial Wear them home before you commit We send you out in a trial pair and see how they feel after a real day, then adjust the lens or the power at the follow-up.
Book an eye exam
Your record We keep what worked Once we land on a lens that fits, it stays on file. Your next supply starts from the lens that already worked rather than from scratch.
About contact lens exams

The lens types we fit

Grouped by what your eyes need.

Most people fall into one of these three. Which one is right depends on your prescription and your cornea, not on preference alone.

01 Everyday soft lenses Daily disposables, two-week and monthly replacements. The straightforward option when your prescription is straightforward.
02 Toric and multifocal Toric lenses correct astigmatism and have to stay oriented on the eye. Multifocals handle reading distance after forty. Both need a careful fitting and usually a follow-up.
03 Gas-permeable and kids' Rigid gas-permeable lenses for hard-to-fit corneas and keratoconus, and first fittings for children, taught properly with handling lessons.

Book a contact lens exam and we will work out which of those fits your eyes.
